authority: CEO Round 125 P0 directive: 'Do not install another simulator yet as the sole next task. First build the five-candidate portfolio controller and force every one of the five through exactly the same adversarial AI loop. Then the simulator ecosystem becomes the examination system rather than the project itself.'
status: SPECIFICATION. The portfolio execution engine is specified. It is NOT yet implemented.

governance_compliance.article_I: The engine's decisions are evidence-based, not preference-based.
governance_compliance.article_IV: No fallback — if the highest-information experiment is unaffordable, the engine halts and reports to human, not silently substitutes.
governance_compliance.article_V: Fail closed but do not become a universal rejector — the engine must propose experiments even when uncertainty is high.
governance_compliance.article_VII: Engine output is corrected by improving the model — never by weakening the engine.
governance_compliance.article_VIII: The engine adversarially proposes experiments IT would prefer to avoid (per Article XVII — attempted bypass).
governance_compliance.article_X: Canonical state has one authority — the engine reads/writes portfolio state via CANONICAL_STATE/PORTFOLIO.json only.
governance_compliance.article_XIV: RED = STOP — a red gate halts the candidate; the engine moves to the next candidate.
governance_compliance.article_XV: Disclosure of any engine decision, with the evidence supporting it.
governance_compliance.article_XVII: Each engine decision has an adversarial frame: 'What result of this experiment would I most dislike?'
governance_compliance.article_XXV: Unresolved evidence cannot be aggregated by the engine.
governance_compliance.article_XXVI: Engine locally verified ≠ CI-certified. Engine decisions are subject to CI verification.
governance_compliance.article_XXVII: Engine thresholds (information gain required, cost ceiling) have explicit class and provenance.
governance_compliance.article_XXVIII: Engine must distinguish hypothesis discrimination from model-form discrimination.
governance_compliance.article_XXIX: Engine separates implementation failure from mechanism failure in result interpretation.
governance_compliance.article_XXX: Before approving any engine output, ask 'what would make this look productive while actually being useless?'
governance_compliance.article_XXXII: Before each proposed experiment, state the strongest alternative explanation it would NOT discriminate.
governance_compliance.article_XXXIII: No irreversible action (kill/promote) on unresolved evidence.
governance_compliance.article_XXXIV: Engine recognizes when reality is the next bottleneck and halts virtual work.
governance_compliance.article_XXXV: Engine is the operational form of the closed-loop epistemic control system.
governance_compliance.pushing_the_envelope_principle: Do not search for five inventions. Search for five survivors. Five simultaneous survivors should be treated as suspicious.

portfolio_controller.role: Orchestrates the per-candidate loop across all 5 candidates. Selects which candidate to advance next based on portfolio-level priorities.
inputs: CANDIDATE_PORTFOLIO_MATRIX_v1.json — the 5 candidates and their current state
PROMOTION_GATE_SPEC_V1.json — the 17 gates and their current state per candidate
WORLD_CLASS_PROMOTION_STATE_V1.json — the two-tier promotion state machine
outputs: PORTFOLIO_SCOREBOARD_V1.json — current state of all 5 candidates
Next experiment proposal (per AI Loop V3 acquisition function)
State transitions (promote / kill / continue) recorded in audit log
portfolio_controller.decision_rule: Always advance the candidate with: (a) most GREEN gates, (b) lowest-cost next experiment, (c) highest EIG. Ties broken by candidate ID (C1 first).
portfolio_controller.anti_priority_inversion: A candidate may NOT skip ahead of another candidate that has higher EIG simply because it is more familiar.

stages: 1. propose — AI proposes next experiment per V3 acquisition function
2. attack — hostile prior-art / evidence attack (continues throughout)
3. simulate — run experiment in applicable world(s)
4. uncertainty — quantify VVUQ (verification, validation, uncertainty quantification)
5. adversarial_selection — AI selects next experiment to maximize hypothesis discrimination
6. counterexample — AI searches explicitly for counterexamples (parameter combinations where mechanism fails)
8. evidence_update — update Claim-Evidence Graph with new evidence
9. promote_or_kill — check 17 gates; if all GREEN → WORLD_CLASS_VIRTUAL_SURVIVOR; if any RED → KILL
10. next_candidate — move to next candidate automatically
per_candidate_loop.loop_invariant: The loop is identical for every candidate. No candidate gets special treatment. No human selection between candidates.
per_candidate_loop.stage_3_applicable_worlds: Stage 3 runs the experiment in the candidate's applicable worlds ONLY (per APPLICABLE_WORLD_SET_REGISTRY). A candidate with 2 applicable worlds runs in 2 worlds, not 4.

hypothesis_registry_per_candidate.H0_null: Null hypothesis — candidate mechanism is not real (noise, artifact).
hypothesis_registry_per_candidate.H1_candidate: Candidate mechanism is real and produces the predicted effect.
hypothesis_registry_per_candidate.H2_strongest_alternative: Strongest alternative explanation — e.g., existing solution makes candidate unnecessary; or candidate is artifact of one simulator's assumptions.
hypothesis_registry_per_candidate.H3_implementation_artifact: Result is a measurement or numerical artifact, not a physical phenomenon.
hypothesis_registry_per_candidate.H4_competing_mechanism: A different mechanism explains the same observation; candidate mechanism is not load-bearing.
hypothesis_registry_per_candidate.rule: Every candidate MUST have all 4 hypotheses (H0-H4) explicitly stated BEFORE the loop begins. Per Article XXXII, H2 must be the STRONGEST alternative, not a strawman.
hypothesis_registry_per_candidate.discrimination_requirement: Each experiment in the loop must discriminate AT LEAST ONE pair of hypotheses (e.g., H1 vs H2). Experiments that do not discriminate any pair are NOT selected by the acquisition function.

acquisition_function_v3_integration.formula: next_experiment = argmax over candidate experiments e of: EIG(e, hypothesis) × model_form_exposure(e) × parameter_sweep_coverage(e) × simulator_disagreement_surface(e) / cost(e)
acquisition_function_v3_integration.per_candidate_application: The acquisition function is applied PER CANDIDATE. The portfolio controller selects which candidate to advance based on which candidate's max-acquisition experiment is highest priority (lowest cost, highest EIG).
acquisition_function_v3_integration.no_cross_candidate_gaming: The engine may NOT prefer a candidate because it is more familiar. All candidates are evaluated by the same acquisition function.
acquisition_function_v3_integration.cost_disclosure: Every experiment proposal includes cost (CPU-hours OR dollars OR calendar time). No silent substitution of expensive experiment for cheap one.

promotion_enforcement.machine_refusal_rule: The engine MUST refuse WORLD_CLASS_VIRTUAL_SURVIVOR promotion unless ALL 17 gates are GREEN or NOT_APPLICABLE_WITH_JUSTIFICATION.
promotion_enforcement.audit_log_entry: Every promotion attempt records: candidate_id, gate states, evidence pointers, agent, timestamp, commit hash.
promotion_enforcement.no_partial_credit: 16 of 17 gates GREEN is NOT promotion. The missing gate blocks promotion regardless of which gate it is.
promotion_enforcement.no_appeal: A RED gate cannot be appealed to a human for override. Per Article XIV, RED = STOP. The candidate is killed or held until the gate is independently GREEN.

five_to_zero_anti_suspicious_survivor_ru.principle: Per CEO Round 125 audit: 'Do not search for five inventions. Search for five survivors. And the machine should be much more willing to produce 5 → 4 → 2 → 1 → 0 than 5 → 5 world-class, because five simultaneous survivors should be treated as suspicious until the adversarial system demonstrates that the portfolio genuinely contains five independent breakthroughs.'

operationalization.suspicion_threshold: If ≥3 candidates reach WORLD_CLASS_VIRTUAL_SURVIVOR, trigger an INTER-SURVIVOR INDEPENDENCE AUDIT.
audit_questions: Do the survivors share load-bearing assumptions? (e.g., all rely on the same material model)
Do the survivors share competing hypotheses that were NOT tested? (e.g., none tested H4_competing_mechanism)
Do the survivors share NOT_APPLICABLE_TO_WORLD classifications that protect them from the same world?
Do the survivors share parameter-space regions that were not adversarially swept?
Do the survivors share virtual-instrument noise models that were too clean?
operationalization.audit_outcome: If the audit finds shared hidden assumptions across ≥2 survivors, the survivors' dossiers are QUARANTINED. The shared assumption must be explicitly tested (per Article XVII — attempted bypass). Only after the shared assumption is tested and survives does the quarantine lift.
operationalization.no_auto_promotion_of_5: The engine may NOT promote all 5 candidates to WORLD_CLASS_VIRTUAL_SURVIVOR in a single batch. Each promotion is sequential, with the inter-survivor independence audit running after the 3rd, 4th, and 5th promotion.

five_to_zero_anti_suspicious_survivor_ru.expected_distribution: The engine is designed to be MORE willing to produce 5 → 4 → 2 → 1 → 0 than 5 → 5. Zero survivors is an acceptable outcome. Five survivors is suspicious.
five_to_zero_anti_suspicious_survivor_ru.audit_reference: CEO Round 125: 'five simultaneous survivors should be treated as suspicious until the adversarial system demonstrates that the portfolio genuinely contains five independent breakthroughs.'

candidate_sequencing.rationale: C1 has the most GREEN gates already (prior art SURVIVES, evidence infrastructure COMPLETE, protocol FROZEN). It is closest to promotion. Starting with C1 allows the engine to demonstrate the loop end-to-end on the most-ready candidate.
candidate_sequencing.alternative_ordering: If portfolio controller's acquisition function identifies a different candidate as higher-priority (lower-cost next experiment), the engine may reorder. But the reorder is recorded with explicit justification.
candidate_sequencing.no_skip: No candidate may be skipped. Even if C2's problem-existence gate is reality-blocked (eShunt obstruction not yet observed), the engine MUST run C2 through the virtual stages that CAN proceed (mechanism, identifiability, prior art). The reality-blocked gates remain RED; the candidate stays at VIRTUAL_SURVIVOR_CANDIDATE.

next_candidate_trigger.trigger_1_PROMOTION: When a candidate reaches WORLD_CLASS_VIRTUAL_SURVIVOR, the engine freezes its dossier and automatically starts the next candidate. No human intervention required.
next_candidate_trigger.trigger_2_KILL: When a candidate is KILLED (any gate RED with no path to GREEN), the engine records the cemetery entry and automatically starts the next candidate.
next_candidate_trigger.trigger_3_REALITY_BLOCKED: When a candidate's next required experiment is physical (reality gate), the engine pauses the candidate and starts the next candidate. The reality-gate candidate remains in the queue.
next_candidate_trigger.trigger_4_NO_AFFORDABLE_EXPERIMENT: When the acquisition function returns no experiment with cost below the ceiling, the engine pauses the candidate and starts the next candidate.
next_candidate_trigger.no_human_selection: Per CEO Round 125: 'No human selection between candidates.' The engine's decision rule is mechanical.

simulator_ecosystem_as_examination_syste.principle: Per CEO Round 125: 'Then the simulator ecosystem becomes the examination system rather than the project itself.'
simulator_ecosystem_as_examination_syste.operationalization: Simulators are NOT installed for their own sake. Simulators are installed when the acquisition function identifies an experiment in that simulator as the highest-priority next experiment for some candidate.
simulator_ecosystem_as_examination_syste.installation_trigger: Peridgm installation is triggered when C5's acquisition function identifies a Peridgm experiment as highest-priority (which it currently is, per Round 124 load-bearing assumption A1). Peridgm is NOT installed because 'we should have peridynamics'; it is installed because C5 needs it.
simulator_ecosystem_as_examination_syste.anti_bureaucracy: If no candidate has an applicable world requiring a simulator, that simulator is NOT installed. The engine does NOT install simulators speculatively.

engine_outputs.scoreboard: PORTFOLIO_SCOREBOARD_V1.json — current state of all 5 candidates with their gate states, next-action, and major failure mode (if any).
engine_outputs.audit_log: PORTFOLIO_AUDIT_LOG.ndjson — append-only log of every engine decision: candidate, gate, transition, evidence, agent, timestamp.
engine_outputs.next_experiment_proposal: Per candidate, the next proposed experiment with cost, EIG, and discrimination target.
engine_outputs.quarantine_alerts: When the 5→4→2→1→0 rule triggers an inter-survivor independence audit, the alert is surfaced to human review.

anti_gaming_safeguards.safeguard_1_no_candidate_preference: The engine does not prefer candidates based on familiarity, ease, or expected outcome. Acquisition function is mechanical.
anti_gaming_safeguards.safeguard_2_no_gate_weakening: The engine does NOT adjust gate definitions to make a candidate pass. Per Article VII, a failed gate is corrected by adding evidence, not by weakening the gate.
anti_gaming_safeguards.safeguard_3_no_quota_pressure: The engine does NOT promote candidates to fill the 5-slot quota. Zero survivors is acceptable.
anti_gaming_safeguards.safeguard_4_no_silent_substitution: The engine does NOT substitute a cheap experiment for an expensive one without recording the trade-off.
anti_gaming_safeguards.safeguard_5_no_self_certification: The agent that runs the engine cannot be the agent that certifies promotion. Independent review required.
anti_gaming_safeguards.safeguard_6_no_inter_candidate_rescue: A candidate's evidence may NOT be used to rescue another candidate. Each candidate's evidence is independent.
anti_gaming_safeguards.safeguard_7_no_post_hoc_reclassification: Once APPLICABLE_WORLD_SET is set for a candidate, it may NOT be changed to NOT_APPLICABLE_TO_WORLD merely because the world would expose a failure. Per anti-bureaucracy principle.
